chapters.title: Foundations and Course Roadmap
chapters.summary: Understand what large language models are, why building them from scratch matters, how transformers fit in, and the staged roadmap of the course; prerequisite-wise, Python is assumed by the reader profile, while neural networks and basic deep learning concepts are introduced only partially and may need reinforcement.

sections.title: Why learn LLMs from scratch
LLMs, generative AI, and the broader AI stack
What modern LLMs do and how they differ from earlier NLP
Applications and motivation
Open and closed models, and learning access
Transformers as the key modern architecture
Tokenization, embeddings, and sequence representation
Attention and long-range dependencies
BERT, GPT, and other model families
The build pipeline: stage one to stage three
Prerequisites, delivery, and current evidence gaps

chapters.title: From Text to Model Inputs
chapters.summary: Learn how raw text is transformed into usable LLM inputs through tokenization, byte pair encoding, token embeddings, positional information, and the full preprocessing pipeline; a gap to flag is that subword BPE mechanics are introduced only indirectly here and may need fuller treatment elsewhere.

sections.title: Why preprocessing exists
Word-based tokenization foundations
Building a simple word tokenizer in Python
Limits of word tokenization
Unknown and boundary tokens in a word tokenizer
Character and subword tokenization
Byte pair encoding as compression
Byte pair encoding for subword vocabularies
Using the GPT-2 tokenizer with tiktoken
Why token embeddings are needed
What embeddings capture
Embedding matrices and lookup layers
Embedding layers versus one-hot plus linear layers
Positional embeddings and input embeddings
Creating next-token training examples

chapters.title: Attention and Transformer Building Blocks
chapters.summary: Understand and implement the core transformer mechanics that turn token embeddings into contextual representations, including simplified attention, causal self-attention, multi-head attention, layer normalization, and residual connections; linear algebra and matrix-shape intuition are helpful prerequisites that are not fully spelled out.

sections.title: From tokens to embeddings and context
Simplified self-attention intuition
Normalization and softmax for attention weights
Computing context vectors
Vectorizing self-attention over all tokens
Why trainable Q, K, V are needed
Causal attention and masking
Dropout, batching, and implementation details for causal attention
Efficient multi-head attention with weight splits
Layer normalization in transformers
Shortcut connections and gradient flow

chapters.title: Assembling and Pretraining a GPT Model
chapters.summary: Build a full GPT-style model, define its next-token prediction objective, train it with a pretraining loop, and generate text with decoding strategies such as top-k sampling; optimization details beyond the loss-driven training loop are only lightly covered and remain a possible gap.

sections.title: What the model is and how the full GPT pipeline is assembled
Configuration, tokenizer, and prerequisite vocabulary concepts
Inputs, batches, embeddings, and dimensions
Dropout, layer normalization, and transformer block internals
Stacking blocks, final normalization, output head, and logits
Coding the model and parameter accounting
Next-token prediction tasks, targets, and basic generation from logits
Loss function: from target probabilities to cross-entropy and perplexity
Preparing data for pre-training
Backpropagation, optimizer steps, and the training loop
Evaluation mode, monitoring progress, and overfitting
Decoding logits into text: greedy, temperature, and top-k sampling
Interpreting decoding behavior and a gap in the course narrative

chapters.title: Using Pretrained GPT-2 and Fine-Tuning for Classification
chapters.summary: Load pretrained GPT-2 weights and adapt the model for supervised downstream classification, including padded dataloaders and a spam-detection head evaluated with accuracy; prerequisite gaps include practical familiarity with PyTorch training workflows and transfer learning conventions.

sections.title: Why load GPT-2 weights and what prerequisites are assumed
Installing tools and downloading released GPT-2 files
Understanding GPT-2 release files, settings, and tokenization metadata
The parameter dictionary and how GPT-2 weights map onto the architecture
Updating the scratch GPT model and assigning pretrained weights
Verifying generation and identifying what can be changed
Preparing the spam-classification dataset
Tokenization, padding, truncation, and dataset design for classification
Building and checking the data loaders
Adapting GPT for classification and making predictions
Accuracy and loss before training
Training loop for fine-tuning
Results, overfitting checks, and what was trained
Inference on new messages and saving the fine-tuned model

chapters.title: Instruction Fine-Tuning and Evaluation
chapters.summary: Prepare instruction-following datasets, load pretrained weights for instruction tuning, fine-tune the model to follow prompts, and evaluate outputs qualitatively and with broader benchmarking ideas such as MMLU.

sections.title: Why instruction fine-tuning is needed and what data it uses
Formatting instruction data into Alpaca-style prompts
Tokenization and variable-length sequences
Batch padding with the end-of-text token
Shifted targets for next-token prediction
Ignoring padding in the loss with -100
The full batching recipe and optional masking choices
Loading pretrained GPT-2 weights for fine-tuning
Downloading and mapping GPT-2 parameters into the model
Checking the pretrained model before fine-tuning
Evaluating a fine-tuned model: goals, examples, and response extraction
Evaluation frameworks for instruction-tuned LLMs
Using Ollama and Llama 3 as an automated evaluator
Improving results and extending the approach
